what: American International Group is a property and casualty insurer. After selling its life and retirement business it now focuses on commercial insurance for large companies, specialty lines such as marine and aviation, and personal insurance for high-net-worth clients.
customers: Large corporations, specialty risk buyers, and wealthy individuals insuring homes, art and yachts.
money: property, casualty and specialty insurance for US companies
commercial insurance outside the United States
moat: Underwriting capacity and a global licence network that lets it insure risks few others will take, built on data from decades of claims.
risks: Catastrophe losses from hurricanes and wildfires can be very large
Commercial insurance pricing has softened after several strong years
Revenue has fallen as businesses were sold
Reserve strengthening on old policies has hurt it before
opportunities: A much simpler company after exiting life and retirement
Underwriting discipline has improved the combined ratio markedly
Large buybacks have shrunk the share count substantially
watch: The combined ratio and commercial insurance pricing.
